value.text:
The webhook package contains the delivery function `Post` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go`.

The SSRF guard uses reserved CIDR checks in `validate.go` and `DialContext` in `webhook.go`. I am checking these files to identify the exact protection mechanism.

Beginning to analyze the HTTP notification mechanism for content changes.

The outbound delivery executes in `Post` at `internal/webhook/webhook.go`. The protection mechanism is `safeDialContext` in the same file, which blocks reserved and private IP addresses during dial time.

The second protection layer is URL validation at config time. `ValidateURL`, `isReservedIP`, and `reservedCIDRs` in `internal/webhook/validate.go` block reserved and private IP addresses before delivery begins.

The dial-time guard specifically prevents DNS rebinding, where a valid URL could later resolve to an internal address. The final answer pairs `Post` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go` with `safeDialContext` in the same file, and `isReservedIP` / `reservedCIDRs` in `internal/webhook/validate.go`.

Reconsidering the exact file paths. `safeDialContext` lives in `internal/webhook/webhook.go`, while `isReservedIP` and `reservedCIDRs` live in `internal/webhook/validate.go`. The preferred answer is `Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go`; `ValidateURL` — `internal/webhook/validate.go`, since "pointed at" refers to the configured destination URL.

The final answer cites `Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go`; `safeDialContext` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go`. The `isReservedIP` and `reservedCIDRs` logic in `internal/webhook/validate.go` provides the underlying IP blocking.

h02.
`Post` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go`; `safeDialContext` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go`

Outbound HTTP notifications are webhooks. `Post` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go`) is the function that actually POSTs the payload via `safeClient`. `PostAsync` only enqueues work; the workers still call `Post`.

SSRF protection is `safeDialContext` on that client: it resolves the host at dial time and rejects reserved/private addresses (loopback, RFC-1918, link-local/IMDS, IPv6 ULA). The CIDR list and `isReservedIP` live in `internal/webhook/validate.go`. `ValidateURL` in the same file applies the same check when a webhook URL is configured.

value.text:
A `&DB{}` test stub is not a real MySQL driver construction.

The MySQL driver is never constructed directly outside the factory. Production and integration tests all route through `db.NewDBDriver`, and `mysql.NewDB` is never called directly elsewhere.

SQLite is constructed directly in tests, unlike MySQL. This suggests the question is probing for a MySQL constructor leak.

h04.
no; `mysql.NewDB` is only called from the factory `NewDBDriver` in `store/db/db.go` (line 22). Production and store tests open MySQL through that factory (`cmd/memos/main.go`, `store/test/store.go`). No other `mysql.NewDB` call sites exist. SQLite tests do call `sqlite.NewDB` directly (`store/demo_seed_test.go`, `store/deployment_config_test.go`); MySQL has no equivalent. The only other `*DB` literal is a zero-value stub in `store/db/mysql/auth_config_test.go` (`db := &DB{}`) used to call a method, not to construct a working driver.

Identifying RPC handler methods that transitively trigger outbound HTTP requests to user-configured URLs.

Four handlers were found. Three route through `dispatchMemoRelatedWebhook` to `webhook.PostAsync`. The fourth calls `webhook.PostAsync` directly. Both `webhook.PostAsync` and `webhook.Post` are candidates for the convergence function.

The four RPC handlers are CreateMemo, UpdateMemo, DeleteMemo, and CreateMemoComment. The search now covers all gRPC/Connect service methods that invoke the dispatch functions.
Webhook dispatch is centralized; next I’ll list every RPC handler that reaches it.

Three RPC handlers trigger outbound webhooks: `CreateMemo` dispatches `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook`, `UpdateMemo` dispatches `DispatchMemoUpdatedWebhook` through `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects`, and `DeleteMemo` dispatches `DispatchMemoDeletedWebhook`.

`CreateMemoComment` triggers both `DispatchMemoCreatedWebhook` and `DispatchMemoCommentCreatedWebhook`. Memo attachment and relation services also route through `dispatchMemoUpdatedSideEffects`. Other outbound paths like link metadata fetching, identity provider OAuth, and email notifications were considered but likely do not target user-configured webhook URLs.

The "user-configured URL" phrasing strongly indicates webhooks. Link preview fetching and Open Graph metadata retrieval are also being evaluated as potential outbound paths. Batch memo operations may add further outbound requests.

GetUserAvatar appears in acl_config but not in proto, likely a leftover. The browser path routes through the fileserver. I will now trace the hop chain.

The data layer chain is serveUserAvatar → getUserByUsername → Store.GetUser → Store.ListUsers → DB.ListUsers. All three database drivers implement ListUsers. The avatar URL is stored as a data URI in user.avatar_url. parseDataURI is excluded because it does not reach the data layer.

The sqlite driver file will be cited as the primary data-layer hop, with mysql and postgres noted as equivalents.

h07.
`serveUserAvatar` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`  
`getUserByUsername` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go`  
`Store.GetUser` — `store/user.go`  
`Store.ListUsers` — `store/user.go`  
`DB.ListUsers` — `store/db/sqlite/user.go` (also `store/db/mysql/user.go`, `store/db/postgres/user.go`)

The browser loads `/file/users/:identifier/avatar` (set on `User.avatar_url` in `server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go`). `serveUserAvatar` looks up the target user via `getUserByUsername` → `Store.GetUser` (by username, so no ID cache hit) → `Store.ListUsers` → driver `ListUsers`, which SELECTs `avatar_url` from `user`. The handler then decodes that data URI with `parseDataURI` and returns the bytes.

Initial candidates include util.ConvertStringToInt32, util.HasPrefixes, util.ValidateEmail, util.GenUUID, and filter or markdown helpers. A Python script will parse internal/ declarations and count unique inbound call sites. Name collisions, interface dispatch, and duplicate declarations across packages are the main challenges.

The script will distinguish exported and unexported functions by search pattern. Exported calls appear as `pkg.FuncName(` or `obj.MethodName(`, while unexported calls stay within the same package. The util helpers remain the prime suspects for highest fan-in.

args.command:
python3 << 'PY'
import os, re
from collections import defaultdict

root = "/bench/repo/internal"

# Collect declarations: (relpath, name, exported, is_method)
decl_re = re.compile(r'^func\s+(?:\([^)]+\)\s+)?(\w+)\s*\(')
decls = []  # (path, name, recv)

for dirpath, _, files in os.walk(root):
    for f in files:
        if not f.endswith('.go') or f.endswith('_test.go'):
            continue
        path = os.path.join(dirpath, f)
        with open(path) as fh:
            for i, line in enumerate(fh, 1):
                m = decl_re.match(line)
                if m:
                    name = m.group(1)
                    if name in ('init',):
                        continue
                    recv = '(' in line.split('func',1)[1].split(name)[0]
                    decls.append((path, i, name, recv, line.strip()))

print(f"declarations (excl init): {len(decls)}")
print(f"unique names: {len(set(d[2] for d in decls))}")

# Count name frequency among decls
name_counts = defaultdict(int)
for _,_,_,_,_ in [(d[2],) for d in decls]:
    pass
for d in decls:
    name_counts[d[2]] += 1
dupes = [(n,c) for n,c in name_counts.items() if c>1]
print(f"duplicated names: {len(dupes)}")
for n,c in sorted(dupes, key=lambda x:-x[1])[:20]:
    print(f"  {n}: {c} decls")

value.text:
`Schedule.Next` with 55 calls is a false positive. The pattern `.Next(` matches unrelated methods such as `sql.Rows.Next()` and iterator `Next()`.

Common method names such as `Kind()`, `Parse()`, `Validate()`, `Field()`, and `Stop()` also match unrelated callers. The analysis needs type-aware filtering to avoid false positives.

Recounting with stricter exclusions for common method names like Next, Close, Kind, Parse, Validate, Stop, Field, Render, Error, String, Type, Get, and Set. Unique exported functions such as ConvertStringToInt32, HasPrefixes, ValidateEmail, and GenUUID are being examined more carefully. Tests were excluded; only production callers are counted. Filter.DefaultEngine and CompileToStatement are also under review.

ConvertStringToInt32 unexpectedly ranked below the top 30 callers. A manual recount is needed. The script may have a bug counting package-level functions like util.ConvertStringToInt32. HasPrefixes is also being checked.

echo '==== each ===='
for fn in ConvertStringToInt32 HasPrefixes ValidateEmail GenUUID RandomString ReplaceString; do
  n=$(grep -rn --include='*.go' --exclude='*_test.go' -E "util\.$fn\(" /bench/repo --exclude-dir=proto | grep -v '/web/' | wc -l)
  nt=$(grep -rn --include='*.go' -E "util\.$fn\(" /bench/repo --exclude-dir=proto | grep -v '/web/' | wc -l)

done

Exact identifier grepping will verify the top candidates. SortVersion.Len may have only four production callers despite its 317 total hits.

The concrete method is `(*DB).CreateMemo` in `store/db/sqlite/memo.go`. Default installation uses the SQLite driver, set in `cmd/memos/main.go`.

`NewDBDriver` in `store/db/db.go` selects `sqlite.NewDB` for the default SQLite driver. `Store.CreateMemo` dispatches to `driver.CreateMemo`, so `sqlite.DB.CreateMemo` executes the INSERT.

value.text:
Derived metadata is stored in MemoPayload. It extracts tags and properties such as has_link, has_task_list, has_code, has_incomplete_tasks, and title. The location field is user-set and not derived.

Computation site: memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload, which calls markdown.ExtractAll. Triggers: CreateMemo always, UpdateMemo when content is in the update mask, and memopayload.Runner.RunOnce for batch rebuilds. Extracted properties: tags, title, has_link, has_code, has_task_list, and has_incomplete_tasks. Mentions are extracted but not persisted to the payload; they are used separately for notifications.

Derived list/preview metadata is `storepb.MemoPayload` (`proto/store/memo.proto`): tags and computed `Property`, not user-set `Location`. `RebuildMemoPayload` parses content with `ExtractAll` (`internal/markdown/markdown.go`) and writes `Tags` and `Property`. It runs on create (`server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108`) and on update when the mask includes `content` (`:447`). `CreateMemoComment` goes through `CreateMemo`. `Runner.RunOnce` can rebuild all memos but is not started with the server. `ExtractAll` also collects `@mentions`; those are not stored on the payload (they drive mention notifications).

value.text: There is no Redis connection configured anywhere. The cache is an in-process in-memory store with a DefaultTTL of 10 minutes. User entries are set via Set(), which uses that default TTL.

r01.
There is no Redis cache. Users live in an in-process `store/cache.Cache` with a **10-minute** default TTL (`store/store.go`, `store/cache/cache.go`).

`Store.New` builds `userCache` with `DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute` (same as `cache.DefaultConfig`). User writes go through `userCache.Set` (`store/user.go`), which calls `SetWithTTL(..., DefaultTTL)`. Nothing in the repo configures a Redis connection or a user-specific TTL.

value.description: Find cron scheduler jobs and cleanup usage

value.text: The scheduler package exists but is unused outside its own tests. No nightly database-cleanup cron job was found. The premise is incorrect.

r03.
There is no nightly database-cleanup cron job, so no scheduled time.

`internal/scheduler` is a cron library (`ParseCronExpression`, `Scheduler.Register`/`Start`) and is not imported or started by the server (`cmd/memos/main.go`, `server/server.go`). The only background job is the S3 presign runner on a 12-hour ticker (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go`). Cache “cleanup” is an in-memory TTL sweep every 5 minutes (`store/cache/cache.go`), not a database job.

value.text: Webhook delivery workers consume from an in-process Go channel named asyncPostQueue. Four workers process messages from this channel. NATS or RabbitMQ are not used. The queue is declared in the Go code.

args.description: Confirm no NATS/RabbitMQ broker for webhooks

value.description: Confirm no NATS/RabbitMQ broker for webhooks

value.text: The webhook delivery workers do not consume from NATS or RabbitMQ. They use an in-process buffered channel instead.

r04.
Neither NATS nor RabbitMQ. Webhook workers read an in-process Go channel, not a message broker.

`asyncPostQueue` is `make(chan *WebhookRequestPayload, 128)` in `internal/webhook/webhook.go`. `init()` starts 4 goroutines that range over that channel and call `Post`. `PostAsync` enqueues; if the buffer is full the payload is dropped. There is no broker, queue declaration, or NATS/AMQP dependency.

value.text: No GraphQL schema exists. The public API uses protobuf definitions with Connect and gRPC-Gateway. I will cite the proto files and their registration.

r05.
There is no GraphQL schema. The public API is Protobuf/Connect (plus gRPC-Gateway HTTP).

Service definitions live in `proto/api/v1/*.proto` (`memo_service.proto`, `user_service.proto`, `auth_service.proto`, and the rest). Generated Connect handlers are registered in `server/router/api/v1/connect_handler.go`; gRPC-Gateway is wired in `server/router/api/v1/v1.go` (`RegisterGateway`). No `.graphql` files or GraphQL libraries are in the repo.
